def factor_tail_skew_conditional_downside_volume(df):
    """Tail skew interacted with median-gated downside volume participation."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    close = df_copy["close"]
    volume = df_copy["volume"]
    ret = close.pct_change()
    skew = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=30).skew()
    down_vol = volume.where(ret < 0, 0.0).rolling(60, min_periods=30).sum()
    total_vol = volume.rolling(60, min_periods=30).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    down_ratio = down_vol / total_vol
    down_median = down_ratio.rolling(60, min_periods=30).median()
    gate = np.where(down_ratio > down_median * 1.2, 0.7, 1.0)
    factor = -skew * down_ratio * gate
    factor = factor.clip(lower=-3, upper=3)
    df_copy["factor_tail_skew_conditional_downside_volume"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_tail_skew_conditional_downside_volume"]
description: Mutates factor_crash_tail_skew_volume_asymmetry by preserving the core crash-fragility mechanism: negative trailing return skew captures fat left-tail risk and is amplified by high downside volume participation. To reduce noise from brief extreme down-volume spikes that can over-amplify the parent's raw modifier and hurt IC/ICIR, this child introduces a lightweight conditional gate: when the 60-day downside-volume ratio exceeds 1.2 times its own trailing median, the ratio is scaled by 0.7. Thus the raw signal is unchanged most of the time, but the volume-confirmation modifier is attenuated in unusually downside-dominated regimes. This keeps one core mechanism and one modifier, returns a continuous raw signal, and retains cross_sectional_transform none to preserve the raw payoff structure.
